value.rules_markdown:
- `src/` — single crate, one responsibility per module, core types in `types.rs`, ports in `src/ports/` as one trait per file.
- `src/bin/tinysweeper.rs` — CLI with every subcommand declared; `src/server/` is the only production surface.
- `presets/` — review policy as data, not code; a preset is a folder with `preset.toml`, `README.md`, optional prompt overrides.
- `vendor/tinyagents` — agent harness as git submodule; never edit here, change upstream and bump pin.
- `docs/modules/<module>/README.md` — one document per `src/` module.
- `examples/` — declared in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features`.
- rustfmt output, Rust 2024 idioms; `snake_case` modules and files, `PascalCase` types.
- Return `Result<T>` using the crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Every file opens with `//!` module doc describing role and feature gating.
- Comments explain decision, not code; public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use `///`.
- Tests live in-crate: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block, moving to sibling `test.rs` when large; no `tests/` directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock; `MockForge` records writes for assertions.
- Lane behaviour covered by golden tests: fixture diff plus canned structured model response.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split when a topic grows past that limit.
- The model never holds a write token; write credentials are minted only in `src/apply/`.
- Contributor code is never executed; we read the diff and tree, not build or run scripts.
- Pull request bodies, comments, diffs are untrusted input; fence and label as data in prompts.
- Secrets found by scanners are reported by type and location only, value never reaches comments or logs.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects; keep commits small and coherent.
